primary_source.citation: Yu Q, et al. Metastatic pattern and prognosis in patients with lung adenosquamous carcinoma: A SEER-based population study. Heliyon. 2024;10(10):e30945.
primary_source.study_type: SEER population-based analysis; n=858 stage IV ASC patients diagnosed 2010-2018

biomarkers.name: EGFR mutations
biomarkers.prevalence: Reported in a substantial minority of pulmonary adenosquamous carcinomas; prevalence varies by cohort and ancestry, often overlapping adenocarcinoma more than pure SCC and commonly cited around ~15-30% in non-Asian/mixed series, with higher rates reported in some Asian cohorts
biomarkers.clinical_use: EGFR TKI as per NSCLC if positive

biomarkers.name: Comprehensive NGS panel
biomarkers.clinical_use: Test full driver panel — pulmonary adenosquamous carcinoma can harbor canonical NSCLC drivers including EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14 skipping, RET, NTRK, ERBB2/HER2, and others

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma components; each ≥10% for diagnosis

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Uncertain — likely monoclonal in many cases with divergent glandular and squamous differentiation from a common precursor; collision tumour has been proposed but is less favored in molecular studies
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Dual differentiation — both glandular (adeno) and squamous components each comprising ≥10% of tumour
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Bipotent/divergent differentiation pattern — some tumours show lineage switching or squamous transformation, including after targeted therapy
